reasonsRejected: no existing session/request-scoped factory-binding convention anywhere else in this codebase; every accepted contract uses explicit call-site parameters
hides the authorization boundary one indirection away from the call site, reducing reviewability of a missing/wrong scope

materially larger and less mechanical caller-migration diff (must also decide construction lifetime/threading of the port instance)

contractRequirements.tenantContextSource: MUST be an already authorization-validated clinic scope. A raw/unvalidated req.user.clinicId or JWT clinic-claim default is NOT by itself sufficient authorization - it is a UI/session default selection, not proof of current access. Must be resolved via resolveEffectiveClinicId(user, requestedClinicId?), validateAndGetClinicIdScope(user, selectedClinicId, res), getAccessibleClinicIds(user) (all server/src/utils/clinicScope.ts), or an equivalent record-derived validation whose own lookup where-clause was already scoped to organizationId + allowedClinicIds (e.g. patientPrivacy.ts's resolvePatient()). No caller may pass an arbitrary clinicId sourced directly from body/query/JWT-default without that validation step. The facade receives an already-authorized clinicId as an opaque trusted value and applies it in every DB predicate, but does not itself re-run authorization - it is a fail-closed data boundary, not the authorization boundary.
contractRequirements.principalSystemDistinction: principal (interactive) callers must resolve clinicId via one of the validated mechanisms above - never the unvalidated req.user.clinicId/JWT claim taken as-is. system/lifecycle (batch job) callers obtain clinicId from a trusted, single-clinic DB iteration/request record, never a system wildcard/bypass value; no such caller exists in this codebase today (see callerClinicIdSourceVerification). Both categories require an explicit, single-clinic-scoped, already-validated clinicId per call; multi-clinic jobs call once per independently resolved clinic; no bypass/wildcard value exists for either category.
contractRequirements.failClosedDbPredicates: clinicId included as a top-level predicate in every read (findFirst where: {id, clinicId, study:{clinicId}}) and every write (update/updateMany where: {id, clinicId, study:{clinicId}} - read and write predicates identical, never a reduced {id, clinicId}-only write predicate); zero-row result on mismatch, never a post-fetch-only comparison
contractRequirements.noCrossTenantExistenceLeakage: ImagingNotFoundError remains the single undifferentiated error for not-found, denormalization-mismatch, and cross-tenant-mismatch cases; no distinguishable shape/timing/message across causes
contractRequirements.auditOwnership: unchanged - remains with the calling service; port performs no audit/activity-log writes
contractRequirements.systemLifecycleCallerRules: system/lifecycle callers scoped per-clinic per-call via their own existing iteration; no multi-clinic single call permitted
contractRequirements.dtoStorageKeyExposure: unchanged from F2-IMPL-001-A's accepted ImagingLifecycleImageDto; no new field added or removed by this amendment
contractRequirements.callerMigrationImplications: mechanical: each of the 3 current direct-Prisma callers (patientAnonymization.ts, orphanFileInspection.ts, deletionReviewInventory.ts) already resolves clinicId earlier in its own call chain; migration threads that value as a new leading argument, replacing the direct Prisma call. Remains Stage 3 work, not performed by this amendment or by F2-IMPL-001-A's re-implementation.
contractRequirements.backwardCompatibility: no production backward-compatibility obligation - F2-IMPL-001-A (PR #304) has zero callers and is unmerged; this is a pre-merge contract correction, not a breaking API change
contractRequirements.rollback: documentation-only revert of this proposal (no app/schema/CI file touched); rollback of a future re-implementation remains single-file delete/revert per F2-IMPL-001-A's own established rollback plan
requiredTests: cross-tenant rejection, case A (markStorageMissing, redactForAnonymization, checkImageStorageExists): call with Clinic A's authorized clinicId + Clinic B's valid imageId -> ImagingNotFoundError, indistinguishable from genuinely-missing imageId
cross-tenant rejection, case B (getImagesForLifecycleReview): call with Clinic A's authorized clinicId + Clinic B's patientId -> empty result array, no Clinic B data
same-clinic success unaffected - full existing assertion suite re-run with correct clinicId
no existence side-channel across all not-found causes
corrected signature-arity assertions (markStorageMissing.length===2, redactForAnonymization.length===3, checkImageStorageExists.length===2 with no 3rd parameter present)

prismaCapabilityVerification.finding: ImagingImageWhereUniqueInput = Prisma.AtLeast<{ id?, clinicId?, studyId?, ..., study?: XOR<ImagingStudyScalarRelationFilter, ImagingStudyWhereInput>, ... }, "id"> - this generated client supports Prisma's extended-whereUnique combination of the unique field (id) with additional non-unique filters, including the study:{clinicId} relation filter, on a single-record update/delete, not only on updateMany. updateMany's own ImagingImageWhereInput independently supports the identical relation filter with no uniqueness constraint at all.
prismaCapabilityVerification.conclusion: the exact predicate {id: imageId, clinicId, study: {clinicId}} is directly usable, unmodified, on either a singular update/delete or an updateMany call against ImagingImage in this repository; no reduced/alternate write-side predicate is required - read and write predicates must be identical (see contractRequirements.failClosedDbPredicates)
